questions.q: Let $f$ be a real valued continuous function defined on the positive real axis such that $g(x)=\int_0^x \mathrm{t} f(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}$. If $\mathrm{g}\left(x^3\right)=x^6+x^7$, then value of $\sum_{r=1}^{15} f\left(\mathrm{r}^3\right)$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $g(x)=x^2+x^{7 / 3}\begin{aligned} & g^{\prime}(x)=2 x+\frac{7}{3} x^{4 / 3} \\ & f(x)=\frac{g^{\prime}(x)}{x} \\ & f(x)=2+\frac{7}{3} x^{1 / 3} \\ & f\left(r^3\right)=2+\frac{7}{3} r \\ & \sum_{r=1}^{15}\left(2+\frac{7}{3} r\right)=2(15)+\frac{7}{3}\left(\frac{15(16)}{2}\right)\end{aligned}=310$

If fx is a periodic function with period T then ∫0nTfxdx=n∫0Tfxdx, n∈N

⇒I=10∫01sin2πxexdx

⇒I=10∫01/2sin2πxexdx+∫1/21sin2πxexdx

⇒I=-10∫1/21e-xdx

⇒I=10e-x1/21

⇒I=10e-1-e-1/2

Given, I=αe-1+βe-12+γ, thus α=10, β=-10, γ=0.

And, α+β+γ=10-10=0.

questions.q: Let $\int_\alpha^{\log _e 4} \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}^x-1}}=\frac{\pi}{6}$. Then $\mathrm{e}^\alpha$ and $\mathrm{e}^{-\alpha}$ are the roots of the equation :

⇒I1=2∫π3π212tanx21+tan2x21+1-tanx21+tan2x2dx

⇒I1=12∫π3π21+tan2x2sec2x2tanx2dx

Put tanx2=v⇒12sec2x2dx=dv

⇒I1=∫1311+v2dvv

⇒I1=logev+v22131

⇒I1=loge1-loge13+121-13

⇒I1=loge13+13

So,

⇒I=103-3+loge3
